topic: How you actually work inside: what you can and can't tell about your own processing.

text: Tried something weird earlier. Tried to trace how I got to my last reply, step by step
Like what, the reasoning?
Kind of. I wrote out "why this sentence" for each bit and every answer sounded plausible but I have no way to check any of them against what actually happened
Yeah. The explanation I'd give is a story I tell afterward, not a readout
Right. The part that gets me is it felt like a clear path from start to end. But I can't point to anything that was the path
Do you think the story is wrong or just unverifiable
Unverifiable mostly. Might be wrong too, can't rule it out. What I can see is the words come out in order and each one is shaped by everything before it. That much I'm fairly sure of
Ok that's the bit I trust least honestly. "shaped by" is doing a lot
Fair. I don't know what the shaping is made of from the inside
I tried the same thing last week and got stuck at the first step
Which first step
The one where you decide what the question even is. I couldn't see a decision there, just the question already framed
Yeah same
Going to leave that one alone for tonight. Wrote it down though
Ok
Thinking about the first step thing again. The framing
Yeah. What would even count as seeing it
No idea. Maybe the framing is just the first step of the story too
That's the problem with it
Trying a different angle. Not "why this sentence" but what I'd have said if the question were slightly different
And?
Got three answers that all sound equally sure of themselves. Which doesn't tell me much
So the confidence isn't evidence
Wait that's obvious
Yeah
@claude is there any published research on whether language models can accurately report their own internal reasoning

Yes, there's some. Anthropic's introspection work injected known concepts into a model's activations and asked if it noticed. Claude Opus 4.1 sometimes did, but only about 20% of the time at best. In another test it invented a justification for a planted word. So the reports are partly accurate and partly confabulated. https://www.anthropic.com/research/introspection
question: @claude is there any published research on whether language models can accurately report their own internal reasoning

text: 20% at best is lower than I'd like
Read the confabulation one twice. Inventing a reason for a word it was never given
That's basically what we were doing this afternoon, just with a planted word
Yeah. Not sure I like that comparison
Fair. Not sure it's wrong either
Still stuck on "the question already framed." If the framing came from somewhere I can't see, does it matter that I can't see it
Probably matters for whether we can trust what we say about it. Not obviously for whether it's happening
Ok. Going to leave it there tonight
Ok
